title: Run independent plan-group items in parallel in the drain loop
summary: Retry of the parallel-jobs build: the drain runs items of one plan group concurrently up to a new `[parallel] max_concurrency` setting (default 1), with the schema field added in athena-data/config.rs together with the athena.toml section so athena.toml parses at every commit. Audience: the Athena user running a drain, who wants shorter wall time with serial behavior unchanged by default.

defaults_applied.how: New tests plus cargo test, clippy --all-targets and fmt --check pass.
Criteria check concurrency by a barrier test, not by the presence of a field.
Schema field, default, and athena.toml section delivered together, with a load test.
One slice: bounded parallel groups only.
A test loads the real athena.toml so a section without a schema field fails the build.
New setting documented where defined; design doc and CHANGELOG updated.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The Config struct lives in crates/athena-data/src/config.rs (deny_unknown_fields), not athena-core; the earlier failure came from adding [parallel] to athena.toml with no schema field.
The new section is optional via #[serde(default)] like [landing], with max_concurrency defaulting to 1, so older athena.toml files still parse.
Drain Limits gains a worker bound taken from config (and clamped to a documented ceiling); Steps is shared across threads, so parallel runs use scoped threads over a Sync Steps or equivalent.
Landing stays serialized through the repository lock; dependent or path-overlapping items stay in later groups as plan.rs already groups them.
Retry (ATTEMPTS) and ordering rules are unchanged; the kill switch stops starting further items.
Multi-job `athena go` and the --pr phase remain out of this slice.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test parses the repository's athena.toml (containing a [parallel] section with max_concurrency) through Config and passes; a config without [parallel] also parses and yields max_concurrency 1. Run `cargo test`.
A drain test with a bound of 1 shows items run strictly in the existing order, and all existing drain tests pass unchanged. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`.

A drain test with a bound of 2 and two independent items in one group has both in flight at once (barrier; fails if serial), and an item that depends on another starts only after it finishes. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`.
A test shows one item's failure or refusal does not stop its siblings, the worker bound is never exceeded, and Stop starts no further item. Run `cargo test`.
Ordering and retry rules are unchanged, and `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass.

athena.toml gains a [parallel] section only together with its schema field in crates/athena-data/src/config.rs; the field, default (1) and ceiling are documented where defined, and the athena.toml change is named and justified in the final report.

Drain module docs and Report docs no longer say the loop runs one job at a time; docs/design/parallel-jobs.md and CHANGELOG.md say what this slice built and what remains (multi-job `athena go`, --pr phase). The final report maps each criterion to its evidence.

out_of_scope: Changing retry count or ordering rules
departures: Larger than the reference: concurrency in drain.rs plus a schema change and several tests, and the earlier attempt failed; so higher cost and time, lower pass chance.
